target_customer: Pharma and biotech sponsors, CROs and research sites running clinical trials
problem: Clinical trials are slow and costly because patients must visit physical sites. Curebase started with remote and virtual site trials and now sells an eClinical software platform (ePRO, eConsent, EDC, engagement).
business_model: B2B SaaS and trial services for sponsors, CROs and sites
product_category: eClinical and decentralized clinical trial software

founders.name: Tom Lemberg
founders.background_notes: Named founder and CEO in MedCity News (May 2021) and TechCrunch (May 2022). Background not found in opened sources. Handed the company to Storm Stillman in April 2025 per a search result.

founders.name: Storm Stillman
founders.role: Listed founder on YC page, later CEO
prior_employers: Luminist Labs (co-founder and CEO, acquired by DiscernDx)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the only founder. Other sources describe him as COO who became CEO in 2025, so co-founder status is uncertain.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a patient app plus compliant data capture and consent for regulated trials, standard software with high compliance burden.

defensibility.rationale: Trial sponsors lock in per study and compliance certifications help, but many eClinical and decentralized trial vendors offered similar modules.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: CVS Health launched its own decentralized trials unit by 2021 per MedCity News. Curebase cut staff in 2023 and dropped its clinical operations unit to focus on software.

market_need_then: Trials were slow to recruit patients, and a 2018 CTTI summary described Curebase pursuing a fully virtual site model, indicating interest in decentralized designs. The COVID period later raised demand sharply.

branding.domain_note: Moved from curebase.com to curebase.ai (current site), no dated source for the change.

identity.visual_style: Standard B2B software, SOC 2 and CDISC credibility badges

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence of community or merch found. Trademark CUREBASE registered March 2019 per a trademark record.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive cure plus base name, similar to many health names (Couchbase confusion in search), no brand assets found beyond the wordmark.

pivots.to: Software platform only (clinical operations unit dropped)
pivots.why: Trade press said it narrowed on software, details of the reason not opened

outcome_analysis: Curebase joined YC in summer 2018, raised $15M in 2021 and $40M in 2022 as decentralized trials boomed, then cut staff and closed its clinical operations unit in 2023 to focus on software. It remains active with a leadership change in 2025. Funding after 2022 was not found, so the later trajectory is uncertain.
notes: TechCrunch calls the 2022 round $40M without a label, other outlets (Clinical Trials Arena) called it Series B led by Industry Ventures with Acrew and Positive Sum, Gilead strategic. A 2018 seed is reported by aggregators with conflicting amounts (120K vs 2.5M) and is unverified. A search result said total raised was 59M. Competitors: no source dated near 2018 listing rivals was found, Science 37 and Medable exist but only in undated or later sources. Fierce article returned 403.
